transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Amir (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood Product), Evan (Starlight CTO), Maya (Head of ML), Jon (Platform), Priya (Security)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focusing on cost per route, token-level breakdowns, and using per-route dashboards to triage latency/cost.

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood, this is Amir our SE.
00:14 Evan: Hi, Evan here, CTO at Starlight. Thanks for the time.
00:20 Maya: Maya, head of ML — mostly interested in cost and model quality tradeoffs.
00:27 Amir: Awesome. Today we'll go through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown features in Redwood Optimize. We'll also touch on Dedicated vs Hosted for your workloads.
01:03 Amir: Jumping into the Console — this is the usage view, you can slice by route, model, and token type, you can see prompt vs completion tokens, and cost attribution down to API-key and route.
01:30 Jon: quick question, can we map routes to our internal product codes? we need that for chargeback.
01:38 Lena: Yeah you can add tags to routes, or map with the resource metadata. we'll show the tagging UI in a sec.
02:05 Amir: here's a per-route dashboard — shows throughput, p50/p95 latency, token mix, error rates. notice the orange spike around 11am — that's a burst from your recommender route in the data we ingested.
02:40 Maya: that p95 looks high for small prompt sizes — are you applying batching?
02:45 Amir: good call. By default the runtime does continuous batching, but per-route batching policies can be overridden. for low-latency storefront calls we'd recommend small max_batch and a latency SLO.
03:10 Evan: what's the unit economics there, how do we estimate cost impact of lowering batch size?
03:18 Amir: in the cost breakdown page you can toggle quantization profiles and batching settings. you'll see estimated tokens per second and per-token cost. the console also simulates price delta between hosted and Dedicated setups.
03:50 Sofia: also note prefix/KV cache savings — for conversational or multi-turn, cache hit rates show up on the route level as a reduction in billed tokens.
04:22 Priya: on security — we need audit logs and KMS integration, and long-term retention for logs. does the console let us export audit trail?
04:32 Amir: yes — audit logs can be exported to your S3 or to your SIEM via webhooks. we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated.
04:50 Priya: any SOC2 artifacts or pen-test history you can share?
04:55 Sofia: we'll send the security packet after this call — includes SOC2 summary, ISO checklist, and our pen test notes.
05:15 Amir: back to cost — here's a route-level cost heatmap. routes are ranked by cost/time. you can group by model or by environment (prod/staging).
05:45 Maya: for our recommender route, we run a 1.5k token context for some backfill — how will that show up?
05:52 Amir: you'll see per-call token histograms and the model selection column; for long contexts it surfaces as higher completion token share and suggests quantization and KV caching where applicable.
06:20 Amir: console also has a forecasting tab — you can project monthly spend given historical QPS and planned changes. there's a controls panel that suggests switching to a quantized variant or a smaller model for lower-cost routes.
06:57 Jon: can we set automated rollouts? like move 10% of traffic to cheaper quantized model and monitor quality?
07:05 Lena: yes, rollout policies support canary, A/B and automatic fallback; Console ties into our tracing hooks so you can see quality regressions tied to a prompt set.
07:35 Evan: another concern is data residency — our EU customers must not leave region.
07:42 Amir: you can pin routes to region and Redwood supports region-aware routing. for Private we can set the control plane in your VPC.
08:05 Maya: show me an example cost calc for the top 3 routes.
08:10 Amir: sure — pulling the sample report... (screen) so route A is the storefront chat, 250 rps peak, avg 60 tokens prompt and 40 completion, costs X; route B recommender is 5 rps but 1200 tokens avg so it dominates token cost.
08:52 Maya: that matches our expectation. can the console show cost per inference in USD and per 1k calls?
08:58 Amir: yes both; the billing view can export csv for chargeback.
09:20 Jon: what about cost smoothing for bursty traffic? we want predictable monthly bills.
09:28 Sofia: that's where Dedicated reserved capacity and burst options help — we gave examples in the deck. committed monthly capacity smooths unit costs.
10:00 Evan: what's the typical uplift in ops to run Private vs Hosted?
10:06 Amir: Private requires infra ops work for the control plane in your VPC — we provide Terraform snippets and an on-prem bundle. Dedicated reduces that as it's managed but isolated. we'll share the matrix.
10:40 Priya: encryption at rest for embeddings — does Redwood support KMS per-tenant?
10:46 Amir: yes, customer-managed keys for embeddings and model artifacts in Private; Dedicated can be configured with KMS as well.
11:10 Maya: can we run a benchmark with our prompts to compare latency between Hosted and Dedicated?
11:15 Amir: absolutely. we'll spin up a pilot with sample traffic and run A/B. we'll need your prompt set and traffic profile.
11:35 Sofia: to recap — we'll send pricing/commit scenarios, security packet, and Amir will put together a pilot plan.
11:50 Evan: sounds good. one more thing — competitors? we were comparing to OpenAI endpoints and also some internal self-host. how do you usually differentiate on cost?
12:05 Sofia: we show per-token profiling and kernel-level optimizations; Optimize suggests quantization and batching and gives estimated cost deltas vs public APIs.
12:35 Maya: ok. timeline — we want to decide by mid-June for a Q3 pilot.
12:42 Sofia: we can meet that. schedule the benchmark next week.
13:00 Amir: I'll upload a pilot test plan doc and a terraform snippet to the shared drive; link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/pilot-starlight (note: placeholder)
13:20 Jon: thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-recognized terms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash), product names sometimes split (Red wood vs Redwood).

End meeting.
